claim: Hibernation signals the operating system to suspend to disk, which saves the contents of RAM to the EBS root volume; when the instance starts again the root volume is restored, the RAM contents are reloaded and the instance keeps its instance ID.

values.spoken: hibernation saves the RAM to the EBS root volume

values.display: the RAM contents are reloaded
the instance retains its instance ID

evidence.quote: When you hibernate an instance, the operating system is signaled to perform hibernation (suspend-to-disk), which saves the contents from the instance memory (RAM) to your Amazon EBS root volume. The instance's Amazon EBS root volume and any attached Amazon EBS data volumes are persisted. When you start your instance, the Amazon EBS root volume is restored to its previous state and the RAM contents are reloaded. Previously attached data volumes are reattached and the instance retains its instance ID.
